models_comparison.notes: Best value small model. Replaced GPT-3.5-turbo. Excellent for high-volume low-complexity tasks. Best price/quality ratio for simple agent steps.
Most consistent and reliable for n8n workflows per community consensus. Handles structured data and tool calling well. Good as primary agent LLM.
Newer model (2025-2026), improved over GPT-4o at lower cost. 1M token context window. Excellent for agent workflows.
Comparable to GPT-4o-mini in quality. Strong JSON/tool use. Popular for n8n classification tasks. Claude Haiku 4.5 now at $1/$5.
Top-tier coding and reasoning quality. Best for reasoning-heavy agent steps. Claude Code is best coding agent. Recommended as primary n8n agent LLM for quality.
Cheapest managed API. Free on Google AI Studio. Best for prototyping and bulk tasks. Flash-Lite at $0.02/$0.40 even cheaper.
Improved reasoning over 2.0 Flash. Best price/quality ratio for production agents. Free on AI Studio for prototyping.
Cheapest frontier-quality model. ~80% cheaper than GPT-4o-mini. Strong reasoning. V3.2-exp available. Excellent for cost-sensitive agent deployments.
Groq LPU delivers fastest inference. Llama 3.3 70B is best free model for n8n per community. Speed unbeatable. Limited context window.
Good function calling support. Mistral Small at $0.10/$0.30 for budget tasks. Nemo at $0.03/$0.06 for cheapest option.
Lowest verified output-token price. Best for simple classification/routing. Quality limited for complex tasks.

Support both stdio (local) and HTTP/SSE (remote) transports
Dockerize for consistent deployment and security isolation
Implement proper error handling and rate limiting
Use environment variables for credentials, never hardcode secrets
Test with MCP Inspector tool before deploying

Remote MCP servers preferred for production (accessible over network)

Chain MCP tools with n8n Agent node for autonomous workflows
Use Docker for self-hosted MCP servers to avoid permission issues
security: Only use Official or Verified MCP servers - avoid untrusted code
Run MCP servers in Docker containers for security isolation

Use remote transport (HTTP/SSE) for production deployments

best_practices: Use layered KB design: ingestion → hybrid retrieval → reranking → evaluation → governed semantic layer
Implement freshness policies for document updates
Label data with timestamps and metadata for temporal relevance
Use chunking strategy: 500-1000 tokens per chunk with overlap of 50-100 tokens
Separate knowledge base content from chat memory (different storage patterns)
Implement hybrid retrieval: combine keyword search + vector similarity
Add reranking step after initial retrieval to improve relevance
Regularly update indexed data and remove stale documents
Use GraphRAG when relationships between facts are important
Design content for machine readability, not just human readability

steps: 1. Document collection: Gather PDFs, web pages, APIs, databases, internal docs
2. Preprocessing: Clean, normalize, remove boilerplate, extract metadata
3. Chunking: Split into 500-1000 token chunks with 50-100 token overlap
4. Embedding: Use embedding model (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, Cohere, or local)
5. Vector storage: Store embeddings + metadata in chosen vector store
6. Indexing: Create appropriate indexes (HNSW, IVF_FLAT, etc.)
7. Retrieval pipeline: Query → vector search → reranking → context assembly
8. Evaluation: Measure retrieval quality (precision, recall, MRR)
9. Maintenance: Update stale docs, re-index periodically, monitor performance
